geometry_edits.rationale: Reduce excessive curvature so the object reads as one hall volume instead of two drifting masses.
Preserve the existing longitudinal bend axis while simplifying the section logic.
Replace the folded/cascading roof character with a calmer daylighting hall section.
Keep the section intent aligned to the long-span hall direction.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the broad bend with a milder twist-like continuity adjustment to reduce the perceived split and make one dominant hall axis more legible.
Reduce curvature so the mass reads as a clearer long-span datum rather than a broken zigzag.
Tighten the split so the two parts behave more like coordinated hall/service pieces instead of separated fragments.
Preserve a cleaner single anchor at ground and avoid over-fragmenting the base condition.
Shift the roof/section toward a simpler hall-like section family to better support clear-span gym logic.
Keep the long-span reading aligned with the main hall direction.

rationale: The candidate reads as one continuous object in broad terms, but the four views expose a twisted, pinched split-wing composition with inconsistent support between views. It has some dominant linear gesture and the silhouette is not merely stair-step massing, but the form is not yet a convincing long-span gymnasium hall. The most serious issue is program logic: the mass does not clearly express a clear-span interior, daylight roof section, or a strong subordinate service/entry bar. Ground response is weak; there is no legible public void, court, or undercut responding to the access edge, and the object feels sealed and semantically inward. Because the section/roof logic appears arbitrary rather than hall-like, program fit fails even though the mass has a plausible athletic-object character.
